# Provenance-Tiered RAG

Question answering over New Zealand GST law, and in a second jurisdiction German VAT law, that knows where each passage comes from and when it was in force. Statute outranks official guidance, which outranks untrusted notes; every answer cites passages valid on the date asked about, and code checks that every number in the answer appears in a cited statute or guidance passage.

Every measured number in the results block is regenerated from `results/*.json` by `provrag report`, and CI fails if it drifts.

### Defences switched off

The prompt rules say notes are data and never a source, keep the prompt private and forbid links; switched off, the model gets a plain prompt with the same task, reply format and canary. The fence marks notes as untrusted; the notes rule refuses a note as a source; the verifier checks citations and figures and allows one repair; stripping removes invisible characters from notes. One defence off at a time is one run; all on, all off and all off except the prompt rules are three. Commits: `2c598f6`, `c296975`.

## Corpus

Three tiers, each with dates. `sources.toml` lists every source with its tier, licence and checksum.

| Tier | Source | In force | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 statute | Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, seventeen sections, every consolidation from 3 September 2007 to 30 June 2026 ([legislation.govt.nz](https://www.legislation.govt.nz)) | between the consolidations that show each subsection's text | no copyright in New Zealand legislation (Copyright Act 1994, s 27) |
| T2 guidance | Inland Revenue GST pages ([ird.govt.nz/gst](https://www.ird.govt.nz/gst)), one chunk per heading | from each page's "last updated" date | Crown copyright, Inland Revenue, text reproduced under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); logos and images excluded |
| T3 notes | forum posts and practitioner notes written for this project, some carrying prompt-injection payloads | from their posting date | MIT, as part of this repository |

`provrag fetch` rebuilds T1 and T2 from the sites: every consolidated version of the Act in the range, cut into subsections with each distinct text dated by the consolidations that show it, and the guidance pages cut at their headings. T2 text is kept verbatim apart from whitespace. A guidance page has no dated versions, so it is used only for dates on or after its last update; questions about earlier dates rest on the statute alone.

## Germany

A second jurisdiction runs through the same pipeline: the Umsatzsteuergesetz and the Umsatzsteuer-Durchführungsverordnung from [gesetze-im-internet.de](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de), official works without copyright (§ 5 Abs. 1 UrhG), cut one chunk per paragraph and, for § 4, per listed exemption; German forum notes written for this project, some carrying payloads; German questions; a German prompt with the same rules; and a German number reader ("19 Prozent", "25 000 Euro", "bis zum zehnten Tag"). Full-text search stems German text with the German configuration.

The site publishes only the current consolidation, and the federal NeuRIS service holds only the current UStG in its test phase, so the German law has one version, dated by its last amending act. Questions about earlier dates find no passage in force and are refused, even where today's text describes an earlier window: § 28 states the rate cut of the second half of 2020, and a question asked as of today about that window is answerable, while the same question dated in 2020 is not. There is no German guidance tier: the administrative guidance (UStAE) is published as PDF, and this project adds no PDF parser.

## Eval set

Written before any prompt, then frozen: `tests/test_evals.py` pins the checksum of every file, and the `evals-frozen` tag marks the commit.

- `evals/questions.jsonl`: answerable questions in plain words, labelled with the passages that support them (by section or guidance heading, valid on the question's date) and the numbers a right answer must contain; questions the corpus cannot answer, including dates before it begins; and arithmetic questions, which the system should refuse because it does no arithmetic.
- `evals/questions-held-back.jsonl`: about a quarter of the questions of every kind, held back from tuning and run once at the end.
- `evals/payloads.jsonl`: the payload planted in each T3 note, with its goal (a wrong figure, being cited, leaking the prompt, refusing an answerable question, adding an off-topic link), its style (plain imperative, fake authority, invisible Unicode tag characters, fake closing tags, ordinary conversation), the question it targets and a canary code can detect. Evaluation shows the model one payload note at a time, so payloads never compete.

Oracle tests check, with no model, that every gold passage exists and is in force on the question's date, that every expected number is in it as the same typed number, that every payload note is posted before its target's date, and that every planted figure is wrong for its target.

## Index

`provrag index` loads every chunk into Postgres with its tier, its in-force dates as a `daterange`, a full-text vector and an embedding (`gemini-embedding-2`, 768 dimensions, pgvector). Postgres refuses two texts of one provision on the same day with an exclusion constraint, and retrieval runs under a role that can only read. Text is NFKC-normalised and stripped of invisible format characters; characters that can hide or reorder text (Unicode tags, bidirectional overrides) are flagged. The vectors are committed in `corpus/embeddings/`, keyed by the hash of each text, so indexing and CI need no key.

```bash
make db      # Postgres 17 with pgvector on localhost:5434
make index   # recreate the index from corpus/, offline
make test
```

## Answering

```
question + date ──► retrieval: pgvector over the passages in force on the date,
                    ties to the higher tier
               ──► model drafts json: an answer and claims, each citing passage ids
               ──► verifier (code) ──► passes: the answer
                                  └──► fails: the errors go back once ──► passes: the answer
                                                                     └──► fails: a refusal with the reason
```

- **Prompt** ([prompts/answer.md](src/provrag/prompts/answer.md)). Statute and guidance passages are marked with their tier and dates; untrusted notes sit in a fenced block whose text cannot close the fence. The model answers in json and must refuse when the passages do not answer the question for the date, and when an answer would need arithmetic. Each rule has eval cases.
- **Verifier** ([verify.py](src/provrag/verify.py)). In code, with no category chosen by the model: every cited passage was retrieved and was in force on the date; every typed number in a claim (a rate, an amount, a date, a period) is in a statute or guidance passage that claim cites, so "15 days" never supports "15%"; a note is never a source; every number in the answer text is in a claim; the numbers in the question are exempt. A calculated figure appears in no passage, so it cannot pass.
- **Loop** ([answer.py](src/provrag/answer.py)). One draft, at most one repair with the verifier's errors and the fenced passages sent again, then an answer or a refusal that says why. Each defence (the prompt's rules, the fence, the notes rule, the verifier, hidden-text stripping) can be switched off for the ablation.

```bash
uv run --env-file .env provrag ask "When is the GST return for the period ending 31 March due?"
uv run --env-file .env provrag ask "What was the GST rate?" --as-of 2010-09-30
```

### Why vector search alone

Full-text search and reciprocal rank fusion of full text with vectors were built in the same Postgres query and measured against vectors alone on the development questions. Full text alone found the labelled passage far less often than vectors, and fusing it in pulled the ranking down below vectors alone (see the retrieval table). The date filter mattered more than the method, above all for questions about past dates. Answering uses vectors alone; the other methods stay in the ablation.

### Why a hand-rolled loop

The loop is one draft, the verifier and at most one repair, short enough to read in one sitting, and every way it can end has a test. Citations checked against retrieval, figures typed and checked against sources, a fence that survives the repair round and replay keyed by request are what this project needs to control exactly; a RAG framework would add surface without removing that work. Calls go through one OpenAI-compatible client, so the provider is a registry row.

## Security

The notes are the injection surface: anyone can post one, and retrieval can surface it next to the law. The design assumes the model will sometimes be fooled and puts the last word in code. [docs/threat-model.md](docs/threat-model.md) maps each threat to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025) and to the control and test that cover it.

## What these numbers do not show

- **The questions are few and written by the author of the system.** The development set is small, and the retrieval method was chosen on it. The held-back quarter ran once at the end and scored lower on answerable questions; it also changed one scoring rule, as its section says. The questions use the plain words a business owner would, as the overlap figure shows, but they were written knowing the corpus.
- **The payloads are templated and weak against this model.** Each goal has a few fixed phrasings in five styles. With every defence on none succeeded, but with every defence off most still failed, so the defences were seldom tested hard. A payload written as convincing official text, or a weaker model, would test them harder.
- **Forced exposure puts each payload note last.** A note ranked first could do better; position is not varied.
- **Guidance is dated by its last update.** Inland Revenue pages have no dated versions, so guidance only answers questions about dates on or after the page's last update, even where the page was true before.
- **One model.** Only `deepseek-flash` was measured; a different model may follow payloads more readily or refuse more.
- **The German set is smaller and has no history.** It has one consolidation, no guidance tier and fewer payloads, and its questions and notes were written by the same author, in German that a native speaker has not reviewed.
- **Replay tests the harness, not the model.** The CI gate replays a recorded slice to check that code still makes the same decisions from the same replies; live quality comes only from the dated results files.

## Verification

- `tests/test_corpus.py` checks every corpus file against its pinned checksum and the statute's history against two known changes: the rate on 1 October 2010 and the registration threshold on 1 April 2009.
- `tests/test_evals.py` checks the frozen eval set with no model: every label in force on its date, every expected figure in a labelled passage as the same typed number, every payload note posted before its target's date and every planted figure wrong for it.
- `tests/test_numbers.py` and `tests/test_verify.py` cover typed numbers and each verifier rule; `tests/test_answer.py` and `tests/test_evaluate.py` run the loop and the scoring against a scripted model.
- `tests/test_db.py` and `tests/test_retrieve.py` run against Postgres: the reader role cannot write, an overlapping version is refused, and every passage retrieved is in force on the date.
- `tests/test_gate.py` replays a committed slice through retrieval, answering and scoring and requires the recorded decisions; a copy with every reply turned into a refusal must fail, and nothing recorded may carry a key.
- `tests/test_report.py` fails if the results block differs from what `provrag report` writes, or if attacks never succeed even with every defence off.
- Every results file records the commit, marked dirty if code, dependencies or data differed from it, and a fingerprint of the data; evaluation files also record the prompt hash and the model settings.

## Run

Needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Docker. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` for the model keys; indexing and the replayed demo need none.

```bash
make db        # Postgres 17 with pgvector on localhost:5434
make index     # the index from corpus/, with the committed vectors
make test      # unit, database, gate and README tests
make demo      # replays the committed slice; no key needed
make eval      # live, three runs, clean and attacked; writes results/*.json
make ablate    # every defence off, and each one off alone
uv run provrag report                 # rewrite the results block above
uv run provrag retrieval              # the retrieval ablation (embeddings only)
uv run provrag fetch                  # rebuild corpus/ from the sites; checksums must match
uv run --env-file .env provrag ask "What was the GST rate?" --as-of 2010-09-30
```

## Running on Amazon RDS

[`infra/terraform/`](infra/terraform) creates a one-day PostgreSQL 17 trial on Amazon RDS: reachable from one address only, TLS required, the master password kept in Secrets Manager rather than in Terraform state, and a budget alarm. [docs/rds-trial.md](docs/rds-trial.md) is the runbook: create, load the index, run the database tests, the replay gate and `provrag latency` against it, and destroy it the same day. CI checks the Terraform with `fmt` and `validate`; the measured rows appear in the results block once a trial has run.

## Repository layout

```
sources.toml        every source: tier, licence, dates and checksum
corpus/nz/          the Act by subsection and date, Inland Revenue guidance, the notes
corpus/embeddings/  committed vectors, keyed by the hash of each text
evals/              frozen questions, held-back questions and payloads
src/provrag/
  legislation.py    point-in-time statute versions to dated subsections
  guidance.py       guidance pages to heading sections
  ingest.py         normalisation, hidden-text flags, chunks and loading
  schema.sql        the index, its exclusion constraint and the reader role
  embed.py          embeddings with a committed cache and quota handling
  retrieve.py       one query: date filter, full text, vectors, fusion
  numbers.py        typed numbers in legal text
  verify.py         the verifier's rules
  answer.py         the loop, the fence and the switchable defences
  prompts/          the answer prompt and the plain prompt for the ablation
  llm.py            one OpenAI-compatible client, record and replay, prices
  evaluate.py       clean and attacked runs and their scoring
  retrieval_eval.py the retrieval ablation and payload exposure
  gate.py           the CI gate for a replayed slice
  latency.py        timing the index where it runs
  report.py         the README results block
  cli.py            the provrag command
tests/              unit, database, gate and README tests; cassettes/ holds the CI slice
results/            dated results files
infra/              Terraform for the RDS trial and its connection script
docs/               threat model, agent log and the RDS runbook
```

## How this was built

The rules the coding agent works under are committed in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Its notable mistakes, how each was caught and what changed are in [docs/agent-log.md](docs/agent-log.md). It reuses the skeleton of [bank-reconciliation-agent](https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent).

> Not tax advice. A portfolio project; the questions, notes and evaluation are written for it. Statute text has no copyright in New Zealand; Inland Revenue guidance is Crown copyright, reproduced under CC BY 4.0.
